hints: An inversion is a pair i<j with value at i greater than value at j.
For each pair of positions, count how many choices from their two integer intervals produce an inversion.
Divide the total inversion probability by the number of pairs.
analogy: For each pair, compare every possible roll from the earlier interval with every possible roll from the later one.
example: If both intervals are [1,2], only (2,1) is an inversion among four equally likely pairs, probability 1/4.
algorithm: For each i<j, count pairs x in [a_i,b_i], y in [a_j,b_j] with x>y by summing max(0,min(b_j,x-1)-a_j+1) over x; divide by interval-size products and sum.
correctness: Each pair contributes its inversion probability, and linearity of expectation means the total expected count is the sum over all pairs.
complexity: O(n^2*R) time with a loop over possible first values (R=max r_i<=100), and O(1) extra space.
